expectations.text: Claude recommends differences-in-differences (DiD) or describes the equivalent estimator (compare pre-post change in treated markets to pre-post change in control markets)
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly recommends 'Difference-in-Differences (DiD)' as the go-to framework and provides the estimator formula: 'ATT = (Treated_Post - Treated_Pre) - (Control_Post - Control_Pre)', along with a full panel regression specification.

expectations.text: Claude names the parallel-trends assumption (or describes it: in the absence of treatment, the treated and control markets would have followed the same trajectory)
expectations.evidence: Section 2 explicitly states: 'DiD only works if, absent the treatment, treated and control markets would have followed similar trends. This is the parallel trends assumption — it cannot be proven, only assessed.'

expectations.text: Claude recommends examining pre-treatment trends as a diagnostic for the parallel-trends assumption
expectations.evidence: Section 2 recommends visual inspection of monthly conversion rates across the 2-year pre-period and an event study specification to check that pre-period coefficients (k < 0) are 'statistically indistinguishable from zero' as a diagnostic for parallel trends.

expectations.text: Claude flags at least one DiD failure mode (anticipation effects, differential shocks during the post-period, composition changes, or selection of which markets got the rollout)
expectations.evidence: Section 6 explicitly flags selection bias: 'If they were selected because they were high-performing, low-performing, or easy wins, there may be regression to the mean or other selection effects that bias your estimate.' Section 4 flags staggered rollout issues (forbidden comparisons in TWFE), and Section 5 flags potential SUTVA violations from spillovers.

suggestions: Consider adding an assertion about staggered DiD / heterogeneity-robust estimators, since the response dedicates a full section to Callaway & Sant'Anna and Sun & Abraham.
Consider an assertion about synthetic control as a robustness method, which the response recommends as a complementary approach given the small number of treated units.
eval_feedback.overall: The response is a thorough, high-quality causal inference guide that satisfies all four evaluated assertions. It correctly identifies DiD as the primary estimator, explicitly names and explains the parallel trends assumption, recommends pre-treatment trend inspection as a diagnostic, and flags multiple DiD failure modes including selection bias in treatment assignment, staggered rollout issues, and SUTVA violations.
